options.name: --copyright
options.description: Prints the copyright notice

options.name: --version
options.description: Prints the version of Ruby interpreter
Specifies the input record separator ($/) as an octal number

options.name: -C
options.description: Causes Ruby to switch to the directory

options.name: -F
options.description: Specifies input field separator ($;)

options.name: -I
options.description: Used to tell Ruby where to load the library scripts. Directory path will be added to the load-path variable ($:)

options.name: -K
options.description: Specifies KANJI (Japanese) encoding

options.name: -S
options.description: Makes Ruby use the PATH environment variable to search for script, unless its name begins with a slash. This is used to emulate #! on machines that don't support it, in the following manner: #! /usr/local/bin/ruby # This line makes the next one a comment in Ruby \ exec /usr/local/bin/ruby -S $0 $*

options.name: -T
options.description: Turns on taint checks at the specified level (default 1)

options.name: -a
options.description: Turns on auto-split mode when used with -n or -p

options.name: -c
options.description: Causes Ruby to check the syntax of the script and exit without executing. If there are no syntax errors, Ruby will print “Syntax OK” to the standard output

options.name: -d
options.description: Turns on debug mode. $DEBUG will be set to true

options.name: --debug
options.description: Turns on debug mode. $DEBUG will be set to true

options.name: -e
options.description: Specifies script from command-line while telling Ruby not to search the rest of arguments for a script file name

options.name: -h
options.description: Prints a summary of the options

options.name: --help
options.description: Prints a summary of the options

options.name: -i
options.description: Specifies in-place-edit mode. The extension, if specified, is added to old file name to make a backup copy

options.name: -l
options.description: Enables automatic line-ending processing, which means to firstly set $\ to the value of $/, and secondly chops every line read using chop!

options.name: -n
options.description: Causes Ruby to assume the following loop around your script

options.name: -p
options.description: Acts mostly same as -n switch, but print the value of variable $_ at the each end of the loop

options.name: -r
options.description: Causes Ruby to load the library using require

options.name: -s
options.description: Enables some switch parsing for switches after script name but before any file name arguments (or before a --)

options.name: -v
options.description: Enables verbose mode

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Enables verbose mode

options.name: -w
options.description: Enables verbose mode without printing version message at the beginning. It sets the $VERBOSE variable to true

options.name: -x
options.description: Tells Ruby that the script is embedded in a message. Leading garbage will be discarded until the first that starts with “#!” and contains the string, “ruby”. Any meaningful switches on that line will applied. The end of script must be specified with either EOF, ^D (control-D), ^Z (control-Z), or reserved word __END__. If the directory name is specified, Ruby will switch to that directory before executing script

options.name: -y
options.description: Turns on compiler debug mode. Ruby will print a bunch of internal state messages during compiling scripts. You don't have to specify this switch, unless you are going to debug the Ruby interpreter

options.name: --yydebug
options.description: Turns on compiler debug mode. Ruby will print a bunch of internal state messages during compiling scripts. You don't have to specify this switch, unless you are going to debug the Ruby interpreter
